needs.description: A balanced dry kibble formulated for adolescent dogs transitioning from puppy to adult: controlled-calorie / weight-management formula (since AJ is heavier-than-typical for a Pug), moderate protein to support lean muscle for an active dog, moderate fat, joint-support nutrients (glucosamine-like ingredients listed on packaging), kibble size suitable for short-muzzled (wider, flatter pieces or small bite-sized pieces), and explicitly duck-free. Buy in sizes appropriate to storage and budget (moderate budget). Consider lines from AJ's brand bias when possible (Mars-owned brands) but verify ingredient list for duck exclusion.
needs.rationale: AJ is 9 months (still adolescent) and energetic but weighs 40 lb — heavier than expected for a Pug — so he needs portion-controlled, growth-appropriate nutrition that helps maintain healthy weight while supporting activity. Avoid duck due to allergy.
negatives: Duck
overly-high-calorie adult formulas
very large kibble shapes that are hard for brachycephalic mouths

needs.description: A shallow, wide slow-feeder bowl or mat designed to slow rapid eating and reduce gulping. Shape should be wide/flat to suit a brachycephalic muzzle (Pug) and stable/non-tip. Dishwasher-safe, non-toxic materials.
needs.rationale: Pugs often gulp quickly; AJ is energetic and large for his breed, increasing risk of eating too fast. A shallow wide slow feeder slows intake and matches brachycephalic jaw shape.
evidence: standard: feeding slow to reduce gulping
negatives: deep, narrow bowls
elevated feeders (avoid elevated feeding to reduce regurgitation risk in brachycephalic dogs)

needs.description: Small, soft training treats designed for repeated rewards: small caloric size, high palatability, single-protein options that explicitly exclude duck. Packaged for moderate budget (bulk pouches).
needs.rationale: AJ is 9 months, high activity and strong — active training sessions need small high-value rewards. Must avoid duck due to allergy.
evidence: standard: training treats for young dogs
negatives: Duck
large, hard treats used for training (choking risk / high calories)

needs.family: Measuring cup / kitchen scale for portion control
needs.description: A food measuring cup with clear gradations or a small digital kitchen/pet scale to precisely portion kibble for weight management. Durable, easy-to-clean, and sized for daily measuring.
needs.rationale: AJ's weight (40 lb) suggests monitoring portions is important during adolescence to prevent excess weight gain while supporting growth and high activity.
evidence: standard: portion control for weight management

needs.family: Indoor water fountain or large heavy non-tip bowl
needs.description: A pet water fountain (recirculating) or a large, heavy, non-tip stainless or ceramic bowl to encourage continuous drinking and stay cool indoors. Easy-to-clean filters and quiet pump are preferable for apartment living.
needs.rationale: Excessive heat warning increases fluid needs; fountains encourage drinking and help prevent dehydration in brachycephalic breeds who can overheat more easily.
evidence: standard: ensure constant access to fresh water
negatives: small shallow bowls that evaporate quickly
plastic bowls that retain odors (if allergic to plastic)

needs.description: A leak-proof, portable water bottle with an attached bowl or foldable travel dish for walks, play in the yard, and car trips. Insulated or wide-mouth designs help keep water cooler on hot days.
needs.rationale: With an excessive heat warning and high activity, AJ needs hydration on outdoor excursions to avoid overheating. Portable water makes frequent rehydration convenient.

needs.family: Cooling mat / cooling bed / cooling vest
needs.description: Cooling mat or cooling-top bed and optionally a breathable evaporative cooling vest sized for a small/medium Pug. Non-toxic cooling gel or evaporative fabric; machine-washable cover. Use cooling vest only for active outdoor periods and remove after cooling.
needs.rationale: Excessive heat warning in area and brachycephalic anatomy make AJ prone to overheating. Cooling surfaces and vests provide immediate relief and safer outdoor activity.
evidence: standard: heat mitigation for short-nosed breeds
negatives: heat-trapping beds (thick faux fur)
leashes or gear that cover the neck restricting panting

needs.description: Lightweight, breathable protective boots rated for heat protection plus a paw balm (moisturizing, non-toxic) for after-walk care. Boots should have non-slip soles and be sized to fit AJ's paws; break-in recommended.
needs.rationale: Hot pavement during heat alerts can burn paw pads. Boots protect during outdoor activity; balm soothes and conditions after walks.
evidence: standard: paw protection in high temperatures
negatives: heavy, insulated winter boots (not appropriate for heat)
products with fragrances that can irritate sensitive skin

needs.description: Extra-durable rubber chew toys (thicker, non-porous, 'extreme' grade) and tug toys designed for powerful chewers. Size appropriate for AJ (not a tiny toy), non-toxic, no small detachable pieces, replaceable when damaged.
needs.rationale: AJ has 'strong' chew strength and is energetic — needs durable safe chews to occupy him, prevent destructive chewing of household items, and satisfy jaw-strength needs.
evidence: about: "AJ is very energetic and very strong."
negatives: soft plush toys for unsupervised chewing
toys with small parts that can be swallowed

needs.description: Dish-like or puzzle feeder that dispenses kibble or small treats to slow feeding and provide mental stimulation (durable construction to handle determined dogs). Multiple difficulty levels to rotate.
needs.rationale: High-energy adolescent dogs require mental exercise in addition to physical activity — puzzle feeders reduce boredom and indoor destructiveness, and help with portion control.
evidence: calendar: Fall Shedding Season (indoor enrichment recommended)
negatives: fragile puzzles that break under strong chewing

needs.description: High-durability balls and throw toys sized for AJ, preferably textured for grip and made from non-toxic, strong materials. Consider a ball-launcher designed for mid-size dogs and interactive fetch in the large yard.
needs.rationale: AJ is high-activity and benefits from vigorous fetch/play in the large yard; durable fetch toys resist rapid destruction by a strong chewer.
negatives: small balls that present choking hazards
soft foam balls that shred quickly

needs.description: A well-fitted front-clip harness (padded, breathable, adjustable) sized for a Pug to discourage pulling and protect the neck. Avoid choke collars. Quick-release buckles for easy on/off.
needs.rationale: AJ is strong and energetic; a front-clip harness gives better control without stressing the neck (important for brachycephalic dogs). Apartment walks need safe control around traffic and during hunting season.
negatives: choke or prong collars
tight collars that restrict breathing

needs.description: Durable leash (6 ft) made of strong webbing or biothane plus a longer line (15–30 ft) for safe off-leash training in the large yard. Hardware rated for strong pullers and corrosion-resistant. Consider a hands-free option for running.
needs.rationale: AJ is strong and energetic; reliable leashes/long lines enable controlled exercise, recall training, and safer yard play (also valuable during hunting season and leaf-blower days).
evidence: standard: secure leash for strong dogs
negatives: thin cord leashes that can fray
retractable leashes for high-traffic areas

needs.family: Reflective/LED collar or vest + ID tag
needs.description: High-visibility reflective harness/vest or LED collar and up-to-date ID tag. Light-up accessories for early-morning/evening walks and during hunting season. Ensure tags contain contact info.
needs.rationale: Hunting season and reduced visibility increase risk; reflective/LED gear improves visibility. Apartment/urban walks benefit from added visibility.

needs.description: A properly sized crate that allows standing and turning around (for a Pug), with breathable sides, washable mat, and optional cover to create a den. Use as safe rest area, not punishment.
needs.rationale: Crate training provides a safe retreat, helps with house training and routine adjustments (school schedule), and supports rest for an energetic adolescent dog.
evidence: standard: crate training for puppies/young dogs
negatives: oversized crates that don't feel den-like without partition

needs.description: Supportive foam orthopedic bed with a cooling top or breathable fabric. Removable washable cover. Size to allow AJ to stretch comfortably but not so large that body heat is trapped.
needs.rationale: Supports growing joints (AJ is energetic and heavier), provides restful sleep, and cooling surface helps during heat alerts.
negatives: deep plush beds that retain heat

needs.description: A deshedding tool designed for short-coated heavy shedders (stainless steel teeth, safe for short coat) plus a soft bristle brush for finishing. Easy-to-clean hair removal and instructions to use gently to avoid skin irritation.
needs.rationale: Calendar indicates Fall Shedding Season — Pugs shed heavily; deshedding tools reduce loose hair in the apartment and cut allergens.
evidence: standard: seasonal grooming for heavy shedders
negatives: overly-aggressive metal combs for delicate skin
tools intended for long-coated breeds

needs.description: Hypoallergenic, fragrance-free grooming wipes safe for face, folds, and paws to remove pollen/dust after yard play; alcohol-free and pH-balanced for dogs.
needs.rationale: Fall Allergy Season and yard play mean pollen and grit can accumulate in folds and paws — wipes are a quick way to clean without full baths and help reduce allergen exposure inside the apartment.
negatives: wipes with alcohol or strong fragrances

needs.description: Quality guillotine or scissor-style dog nail clippers sized for AJ plus a nail file/emery to smooth edges. Non-slip grip and safety guard recommended.
needs.rationale: Regular nail care is standard for all dogs; apartment floors can amplify sound and long nails can affect gait. Start trimming frequently at this age to habituate AJ.

needs.description: Dual-headed pet toothbrush or finger brush and enzymatic pet toothpaste in flavors that avoid known allergens (no duck). Toothpaste should be palatable for training acceptance.
needs.rationale: Dental care is standard-of-care — early introduction at 9 months helps prevent tartar buildup. Ensure toothpaste doesn't contain problematic proteins for allergy.
evidence: standard: dental care for all pets
negatives: toothpaste or chews containing Duck

needs.family: Durable dental chews (VOHC or vet-recommended, duck-free)
needs.description: Long-lasting dental chews or chew sticks approved by relevant dental standards (look for VOHC seal), sized for a strong chewer, and explicitly duck-free.
needs.rationale: Supplemental dental chews support daily oral hygiene for a high-energy dog who chews strongly. Must avoid duck allergy.
negatives: soft chews that break into pieces
duck-flavored chews

needs.description: A plug-in pheromone diffuser for the apartment and a snug calming vest (Thundershirt-style) sized for AJ. Use the diffuser continuously and vest during known triggers (leaf blowers, fireworks, hunting season noise).
needs.rationale: Calendar shows Leaf Blower Season and Hunting Season (noise stressors). Pugs can be noise-sensitive; non-pharmaceutical calming products help reduce anxiety during stressful events.
negatives: assuming anxiety medication (do not recommend)

needs.description: A HEPA air purifier sized for the main living area to reduce airborne pollen and dander during Fall Allergy Season. Replaceable filters and quiet operation for apartment living.
needs.rationale: Fall Allergy Season listed in calendar; an air purifier can reduce indoor allergens and improve comfort for both dog and household.

needs.description: Pet-safe enzymatic odor & stain cleaner for urine/feces accidents and high-quality biodegradable poop bags (scented or unscented per preference). Keep supply for both indoor and yard use.
needs.rationale: Apartment living + adolescent dog means possible indoor accidents; enzymatic cleaners remove odors that attract repeat marking. Poop bags are essential for outdoor outings and apartment waste disposal.
evidence: standard: cleaning supplies for pet households

needs.family: Lint roller / pet hair vacuum attachment
needs.description: Heavy-duty lint roller and a pet-hair-specific vacuum attachment or handheld vacuum to manage Pug shedding on furniture and clothes. Pick tools sized for apartment use.
needs.rationale: Pugs are heavy shedders and calendar indicates Fall Shedding Season — frequent removal of hair prevents build-up in a small living space.

needs.description: Simple clicker for marker training plus a hands-free treat pouch to carry training treats during short apartment/yard sessions. Durable construction for frequent use.
needs.rationale: AJ is 9 months and benefits from consistent training (calendar indicates School Year Schedule → routine adjustments). Clicker/treat pouch facilitate efficient reward-based training.

needs.description: A small pet scale or compact bathroom scale plus a plan to track weight trends. Helps ensure AJ stays within healthy weight range during growth and activity changes.
needs.rationale: AJ is 9 months and currently 40 lb — monitoring weight at home allows early detection of excess weight and helps manage portions/caloric intake.
evidence: standard: weight monitoring for overweight/young dogs

needs.description: A basic pet first-aid kit containing bandage materials, tweezers, non-toxic saline wound rinse, emergency blanket, and instructions. Do not include prescription meds; include vet contact list.
needs.rationale: Apartment + yard access increases potential for minor injuries; a first-aid kit provides preparedness for non-medical emergencies and stabilizing until professional care if needed.
negatives: prescription medications (do not include)

needs.family: Shade & sun protection for yard (pop-up shade or umbrella) and pet-safe sunscreen
needs.description: Portable pop-up shade or canopy for the yard and a pet-safe, non-chemical sunscreen for exposed skin (nose, ears) if AJ will be in direct sun. Shade should be stable and easy to move.
needs.rationale: Excess heat warning and outdoor access: dogs with short coats and exposed skin can overheat or get sunburn. Shade and sunscreen reduce heat stress and skin damage.
negatives: human sunscreen with zinc/ingredients not labeled safe for pets

needs.family: Lightweight reflective vest or harness cover
needs.description: A breathable, reflective vest or harness cover to increase visibility during walks in low light and during hunting season. Should be lightweight and not impede panting.
needs.rationale: Hunting Season and evening walks require increased visibility for safety; reflective apparel complements LED collars.
